title: In situ Hi-C Protocol
text:
Scaled master mixes






NoteMath audit — how every volume is calculated





Core formula (all standard mixes):
\[V_{total} = V_{per\_sample} \times N_{samples} \times 1.10\]
Formaldehyde crosslinking — working backwards from 1% final in ~10 mL/sample:
\[V_{16\%\;stock} = \frac{N_{cells} \times 1.1}{0.16} \; mL\]
Glycine quench — to reach 0.2M final from 2M stock:
\[V_{2M\;glycine} = \frac{N_{cells} \times 1.1}{10} \; mL\]
Biotin fill-in — ⚠️ 5% excess ONLY (not 10%):
\[V_{total} = V_{per\_sample} \times N_{samples} \times \mathbf{1.05}\]
Biotin-14-dATP costs ~$800/vial. The 5% exception is intentional and hardcoded.

e   = n_samples * 1.10
e5  = n_samples * 1.05

text:
Day 0 — Crosslinking






WarningFormaldehyde — fume hood only



All formaldehyde steps must be performed in a fume hood. Collect formaldehyde-exposed waste separately for disposal per institutional guidelines. Glycine quench must be added in the hood before moving tubes to bench.








TipCounting cells before crosslinking





Plate an extra well at the same density as your experimental wells and count from that well on Day 0. Do not count from your experimental wells — removing cells for counting changes the density of the remaining cells.

fa = (n_cells_M * 1.1 / 0.16).toFixed(2)
gl = (n_cells_M * 1.1 / 10).toFixed(2)

Inputs.table([

  {Step: "2", Action: `Add 1% formaldehyde (${fa} mL of 16% stock/sample); 10 min RT`,                     Detail: "Fume hood; rock gently"},
  {Step: "3", Action: `Quench: ${gl} mL 2M glycine/sample → 0.2M final; 5 min RT`,                         Detail: "Rock; RT"},
  {Step: "4", Action: "Pellet; wash 5 mL cold PBS × 2; scrape if adherent",                                 Detail: "2500 rpm 5 min 4°C"},
  {Step: "5", Action: `Resuspend 1 mL PBS/5M cells; aliquot ${n_cells_M}M/tube`,                            Detail: "—"},

Day 1 — Lysis & MboI restriction digest (~2 hr + O/N)






WarningMboI handling



Keep MboI in the glycerol block on ice at all times. Return to –20°C immediately after dispensing. Never let it sit at room temperature — glycerol-containing enzymes lose activity quickly when warmed.








NoteWhy 0.5% SDS + Triton X-100 quench?





SDS permeabilizes nuclei to allow MboI access to chromatin. However, SDS also inhibits MboI, so it must be quenched with Triton X-100 before adding enzyme. The 62°C step ensures denaturation of surface proteins without denaturing chromatin structure.

title: In situ Hi-C Protocol
section: Day 2 — Biotin fill-in, ligation & crosslink reversal (~6.5 hr + O/N)
text:
Day 2 — Biotin fill-in, ligation & crosslink reversal (~6.5 hr + O/N)






Warning5% excess only for biotin fill-in — not 10%



Biotin-14-dATP is extremely expensive. The biotin fill-in master mix uses 5% excess (not the standard 10%). This is the only step in the protocol with a different excess factor.








NoteWhy proximity ligation at RT with slow rotation?





Proximity ligation must occur while chromatin is still condensed inside intact nuclei — this ensures only DNA ends that are spatially close get ligated. Elevated temperature or vigorous mixing would release chromatin and allow random intermolecular ligation, destroying the contact information.











Step
Action
Detail




1
Inactivate MboI: 62°C 20 min; cool to RT
Set oven to 23°C (open door)


2
Add 50 µL biotin fill-in mix — 5% excess only
37°C 1.5h rotation


3
Add 900 µL ligation mix; RT 4h slow rotation
Slowest oven speed; door open


4
Spin 2500×g 5 min; remove supernatant
—


5
Resuspend in 546 µL crosslink reversal mix; 55°C 30 min
Thermomixer


6
Continue 68°C O/N; no shaking
—

title: In situ Hi-C Protocol
text:
Day 4 — Shearing & size selection (~6.5 hr)






WarningTarget size is 300–500 bp — verify with gel before proceeding



If shearing is outside this range, the size selection will be off and library complexity will suffer. Run a 1:5 dilution on a 2% agarose gel before proceeding to AMPure. Do not skip the gel check.








TipAMPure size selection logic





The two-step AMPure protocol selects for 300–500 bp fragments. Step 1 (0.55×): large fragments (>500 bp) bind beads, small fragments (<500 bp) stay in supernatant — keep supernatant. Step 2 (add 0.15× more to supernatant): now 300–500 bp fragments bind — keep these beads. Fragments <300 bp remain in supernatant and are discarded.











Step
Action
Detail




1
Qubit BR; if >150 ng/µL dilute to 150 ng/µL in 130 µL
—


2
Covaris LE220: Duty 25 / PIP 500 / 200 cyc/burst / 90 sec
130 µL microTUBE; fill level 6


3
Transfer + wash vial with 70 µL ddH₂O → 200 µL total
—


4
Gel verify shearing: 1:5 dilution on 2% agarose
Use bottom layer of gel

<500 bp in supernatant

300–500 bp on beads

Store –20°C

NoteMath audit — how every volume is calculated





Surface area — the foundation of all ENS volume calculations:
\[A_{total} = N_{wells} \times 9.5 \; cm^2/well\]
Cocktail volumes:



Phase

µL/cm²

Factor dilutions — each growth factor is added as a small volume to E6 base. For Cocktail A, BMP4 at 1:10,000 dilution means: \(V_{BMP4} = V_{total} \times 10^{-4}\)
NC-C medium — scales by number of ULA wells (2 mL per well): \[V_{NC\text{-}C\;total} = N_{wells} \times 2 \; mL\]
Coating volumes (PLO, LM/FN) — 100 µL/cm²: \[V_{coating} = A_{total} \times 0.1 \; mL/cm^2\]





Code
fmt_ens = (x, d = 1) => x.toFixed(d)








Cocktail A — Days 0–2 (200 µL/cm²)






NoteWhy these signals?





BMP4 (1 ng/mL) activates the NC gene regulatory network in the absence of serum. SB431542 blocks TGFβ to prevent mesendodermal fate. CHIR at 600 nM activates WNT to initiate NC specification. Lower CHIR here than in later cocktails — high WNT too early overspecifies posterior identity before NC identity is established.





Code
{
  const vol = total_cm2 * 0.2
  Inputs.table([
    {Component: "Essential 6 (E6)",    Catalog: "Life Tech A1516401", "Final conc.": "base",    "Amount (µL)": fmt_ens(vol * (1 - 1e-4 - 1e-3 - 1e-4))},
    {Component: "BMP4 (10 µg/mL)",    Catalog: "R&D 314-BP",        "Final conc.": "1 ng/mL", "Amount (µL)": fmt_ens(vol * 1e-4)},
    {Component: "SB431542 (10 mM)",   Catalog: "R&D 1614",          "Final conc.": "10 µM",   "Amount (µL)": fmt_ens(vol * 1e-3)},
    {Component: "CHIR 99021 (6 mM)",  Catalog: "Tocris 4423",       "Final conc.": "600 nM",  "Amount (µL)": fmt_ens(vol * 1e-4)}
  ], {layout: "auto"})
}









Cocktail B — Days 2–4 (200 µL/cm²)






NoteWhy the CHIR increase?





CHIR rises from 600 nM to 1.5 µM at Day 2. Once NC identity is initiated, sustained higher WNT signaling drives proliferation and maintains SOX10+ progenitor state. BMP4 is dropped — it is only needed in the short induction window at Day 0.





Code
{
  const vol = total_cm2 * 0.2
  Inputs.table([
    {Component: "Essential 6 (E6)",   "Final conc.": "base",   "Amount (µL)": fmt_ens(vol * (1 - 1e-3 - 2.5e-4))},
    {Component: "SB431542 (10 mM)",  "Final conc.": "10 µM",  "Amount (µL)": fmt_ens(vol * 1e-3)},
    {Component: "CHIR 99021 (6 mM)", "Final conc.": "1.5 µM", "Amount (µL)": fmt_ens(vol * 2.5e-4)}
  ], {layout: "auto"})
}









Cocktail C — Days 6–12 (vagal patterning + retinoic acid)






WarningVolume increases — do not miss this




Days 6–8: 400 µL/cm² (doubles from Cocktail B)
Day 10: 600 µL/cm² (increases again)

This compensates for rising confluency. Insufficient volume at this stage causes monolayer detachment and lost cells.








WarningRetinoic acid handling



RA is light-sensitive and degrades rapidly at 37°C. Always make a fresh working stock from your –80°C aliquot on the day of use. Use amber tubes. Do not re-use opened aliquots.








NoteWhy RA starts at Day 6, not Day 0





Premature RA exposure (Days 0–4) actually inhibits NC induction by over-posteriorizing cells before NC identity is established. RA is only added once CHIR-driven NC specification is underway, then it caudalizes NC cells toward vagal/HOXB3+/HOXB5+ identity required for ENS competence.

text:
Troubleshooting






TipCD49D+ <40% at Day 12





Most likely causes: wrong Day 0 confluency; degraded RA; CHIR lot variability. Check in this order: (1) confirm Day 0 was 70%; (2) make fresh RA from a new –80°C aliquot; (3) titrate your CHIR lot (1–5 µM) in a test well. CHIR activity varies significantly between lots.









TipSpheroids not forming (Phase 2)





Almost always a plate issue — verify Corning ULA certification. If using correct plates, check FGF2 activity (add BSA carrier) and reduce seeding density.









TipLow TUBB3+ at Day 40 (<60%)





Three most common causes: (1) single-cell dissociation at Day 15 — use serological pipette; (2) PLO/LM/FN surface dried before plating; (3) inactive GDNF lot. Test each in order.









TipSMA+ myofibroblast contamination





NC-derived SMA+ flat cells are the primary contaminant. They eventually cause neuronal detachment. Minimize by FACS-sorting CD49D+ at Day 12 if contamination is severe, or by reducing passaging ratio at Day –2.

text:
Working solutions — scaled to sample count






NoteMath audit — how every volume is calculated





CitraHB Complete (10 mL aliquot per sample — used in Steps 2, 3, and 6):
\[V_{aliquot} = 10\;mL \times N_{samples} \times (1 + overage)\]
Additives (SUPERase, RNAsin, spermidine, spermine, DTT) scale linearly with \(V_{aliquot}\); protease inhibitor tablets are whole units, so the tablet count rounds up.
Iodixanol step gradient — each of the three working solutions is made by diluting 50% iodixanol (itself made 5 parts OptiPrep : 1 part Diluent, since OptiPrep ships at 60% and \(5/6 \times 60\% = 50\%\)) down to the target percentage with CitraPrepHB, using \(C_1V_1 = C_2V_2\):
\[V_{50\%\ stock\ needed} = V_{total} \times \frac{\%_{target}}{50\%} \qquad V_{diluent} = V_{total} - V_{50\%\ stock\ needed}\]
Per-sample total volumes (from the source calculation): 15 mL of 50% (kept as-is), 4 mL of 40%, and 7.5 mL of 30%. All three scale with \(N_{samples} \times (1+overage)\).
Polyamine additives in each gradient solution scale as \(V_{total}/1000\) (spermidine, spermine, DTT — 1000X). SUPERase and RNAsin scale as:
\[V_{stock} = \frac{C_{final}}{C_{stock}} \times V_{total}\]
This protocol targets \(C_{final} = 0.5\) U/µL for each inhibitor (not 0.2 U/µL), assuming a \(C_{stock} = 40\) U/µL stock — both are single-source-of-truth cells (rnase_final, rnase_stock) up top, so edit them there if your stock concentration differs.

Nuclei resuspension buffer (30 mL aliquot per sample):
\[V_{buffer} = 30\;mL \times N_{samples} \times (1+overage)\]
Bovine Serum Albumin (BSA) scales as 1% w/v of \(V_{buffer}\); SUPERase and RNAsin use the same \(C_{final}/C_{stock} \times V_{buffer}\) formula above. No spermine, spermidine, or Dithiothreitol (DTT) — these interfere with downstream cDNA synthesis.

text:
Protocol

Tissue homogenization (~30 min)






TipCheck nuclei before proceeding





Step 4 calls for pulling an aliquot to check nuclei release after homogenization — add more strokes with the tight pestle if intact cells are still visible before moving on.











Step
Action
Volume




1

—


2
Cut snap-frozen tissue into small pieces (<0.5 cm) with clean scissors, in a petri dish on ice, in CitraHB complete
1 mL/sample

4 mL/sample


4
Homogenize 20× with loose pestle; add Detergent; homogenize 20× with tight pestle. Pull an aliquot to check nuclei; homogenize further if needed
320 µL/sample Detergent


5
Filter through 40 µM strainer
—





Iodixanol gradient centrifugation (~1 hr + spin)






WarningNo brake on the Step 8 spin



This spin is run on an ultracentrifuge: 18 min at 10,000×g at 4°C with no brake. Braking will disturb the gradient interface and mix layers together, ruining nuclei recovery. Schedule the ultracentrifuge for 18 min run time, but budget closer to an hour for the step overall — loading/vacuum draw-down, acceleration, and the unbraked coast to a stop add substantial time beyond the programmed 18 min.










Step
Action
Volume




6
Add 50% iodixanol solution to the filtered sample (5 mL CitraHB fraction) and vortex to mix
5 mL/sample


7
Underlay sample with 30% and then 40% iodixanol solutions
Per gradient volumes above


8
Weigh conical tubes against each other on a scale, topping up the lighter tube(s) with cell culture grade water dropwise until matched (within ~0.1 g), then place balanced tubes opposite each other in the rotor; centrifuge in the ultracentrifuge for 18 min at 10,000×g, 4°C, no brake
—


9
Collect nuclei from the interface layer with a P1000 pipette; transfer to a new tube
—









ImportantChecklist




Gradient tubes weighed against each other and balanced to within ~0.1 g before spinning
Balanced tubes loaded opposite each other in the rotor
Ultracentrifuge confirmed at no-brake setting
Interface layer collected cleanly, minimal carryover of gradient layers





Nuclei wash & counting (~30 min)








Step
Action
Volume




10
Add nuclei wash buffer in a 15 mL tube; vortex
10 mL/sample


11
Filter through 20 µM filter
—


12
Spin 10 min at 500×g, 4°C to pellet nuclei
—


13
Resuspend in nuclei wash buffer; repeat spin (Step 12)
10 mL/sample


14
Resuspend in nuclei wash buffer; count using hemocytometer (see method below)
200 µL/sample


15
Load for single cell
—









TipHemocytometer counting method



CitraPrep nuclei yields are typically too low for a reliable Countess (automated) read, so this is a manual hemocytometer count every time — do not substitute the Countess.

Filter your trypan blue stock through a 0.2 µm filter before use — unfiltered trypan blue carries particulates that get miscounted as nuclei, and this matters more at low nuclei numbers where a few false counts skew the result.
Mix the nuclei suspension with filtered trypan blue at a 1:1 ratio (e.g. 10 µL suspension + 10 µL trypan blue) — dilution factor = 2.
Load 10 µL of the mix onto the hemocytometer; let it wick in by capillary action, no bubbles.
Under the microscope, count nuclei in the 4 corner grid squares (16 small squares each). Use the standard hemocytometer counting rule: count nuclei touching the top and left borders of a square, but not the bottom or right, to avoid double-counting nuclei that sit on a line.
Calculate concentration:

\[Nuclei/mL = \frac{\text{sum of nuclei in 4 corner squares}}{4} \times 2\ (\text{dilution factor}) \times 10^4\]
Divide by 1000 to convert to nuclei/µL for loading calculations.

Nuclei suspension diluted 1:1 with trypan blue
Nuclei intact and free of debris under the hemocytometer

Loaded for single-cell run at: _______

Cell Suspension Volume Calculator






WarningDo not add PBS directly to the cell suspension



Add PBS to the Master Mix instead — see Step 1.2c below.








NoteMath audit — reproduced from the source calculator table





10x Genomics ships this step as a large printed lookup table (Cell Stock Concentration × Targeted Cell Recovery, CG000731 p.34–35) rather than a formula. Back-calculating from >10 entries spanning both halves of that table gives a consistent relationship:
\[V_{cell\ suspension} = \frac{1.45 \times N_{target}}{C_{stock}} \qquad V_{PBS} = 36.6\;\mu L - V_{cell\ suspension}\]
where 36.6 µL is the fixed PBS + cell-suspension allowance (Master Mix 28.4 µL + 36.6 µL = 65 µL total per tube), and 1.45 is the recovery/loading factor implied by the table (≈69% capture efficiency). This reproduces every checked entry in the source table to within its printed rounding (±0.1 µL). If a computed cell suspension volume exceeds 36.6 µL, that combination isn’t achievable — the source table greys these cells out (“exceeds allowable PBS volume”); dilute your stock or lower the target instead.
Since stock concentration is entered per sample above, this section computes cell suspension and PBS volumes per sample too — each tube gets its own mix even though every tube targets the same cell recovery.

sample_calcs = stock_concs.map((c, i) => {
  const cell_susp_vol = 1.45 * target_cells / c;
  return {
    sample: i + 1,
    stock_conc: c,
    cell_susp_vol,
    pbs_vol: 36.6 - cell_susp_vol,
    achievable: cell_susp_vol <= 36.6
  };
})

Cell Suspension Volume Calculator

NoteMath audit — reproduced from the source calculator table





10x Genomics ships this step as a large printed lookup table (Cell Stock Concentration × Targeted Cell Recovery, CG000731 p.34–35) rather than a formula. Back-calculating from >10 entries spanning both halves of that table gives a consistent relationship:
\[V_{cell\ suspension} = \frac{1.45 \times N_{target}}{C_{stock}} \qquad V_{PBS} = 36.6\;\mu L - V_{cell\ suspension}\]
where 36.6 µL is the fixed PBS + cell-suspension allowance (Master Mix 28.4 µL + 36.6 µL = 65 µL total per tube), and 1.45 is the recovery/loading factor implied by the table (≈69% capture efficiency). This reproduces every checked entry in the source table to within its printed rounding (±0.1 µL). If a computed cell suspension volume exceeds 36.6 µL, that combination isn’t achievable — the source table greys these cells out (“exceeds allowable PBS volume”); dilute your stock or lower the target instead.
Since stock concentration is entered per sample above, this section computes cell suspension and PBS volumes per sample too — each tube gets its own mix even though every tube targets the same cell recovery.

  const cell_susp_vol = 1.45 * target_cells / c;
  return {

    stock_conc: c,
    cell_susp_vol,
    pbs_vol: 36.6 - cell_susp_vol,
    achievable: cell_susp_vol <= 36.6

})

WarningIndex hopping mitigation



Store each library individually (4°C ≤72 h, or −20°C long-term) — do not pool during storage. Pool only immediately before sequencing; an extra 1.0X SPRI cleanup on the pooled libraries can remove residual free adaptors. Never pool two libraries sharing the same sample index in one lane — this breaks demultiplexing.


Compatible sequencers: MiSeq, NextSeq 500/550/2000, HiSeq 2500 (Rapid Run), HiSeq 3000/4000, NovaSeq 6000. Data is analyzed with Cell Ranger (BCL/FASTQ → BAM, MEX, CSV, HDF5, web summary, .cloupe) and visualized in Loupe Browser.
